transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I guess what brings me in is... I've just gotten so, so slowed down lately. I work as an auditor, and we actually just moved to a new floor in our building—which is supposed to be this great open-concept space with all these modern plants, but honestly, the fluorescent lighting is just awful and Susan from payroll is always walking by with these incredibly loud clicky shoes. 

But anyway, I just... I sit there at my desk, and I can stare at one single audit workpaper for, like, twenty minutes. Just staring at it before I even move my hand to type a single number. I used to be so fast at this, you know? Back when I got my bachelor's, I was the one teaching everyone else how to run complex macros... my roommate thought I was ridiculous, but I actually really liked it. Now, though... people at work have definitely started noticing that I’m just not keeping up anymore.
Do you find yourself enjoying things you used to like, such as running complex macros, as much as you did before?

No... not really. Even the macros, they just feel totally pointless now. It's actually like that with everything. I used to do so much on my weekends—I’d plan these big hikes, take my camera out for photos, cook these big elaborate meals on Sundays, and I even volunteered at the local library... which, actually, the library is right down the street from this amazing little bakery. Have you ever been to the one on 4th? They make these sourdough croissants. My old roommate, the one I was telling you about, she used to drag me there every Sunday morning before I did my cooking. She's living in Seattle now, actually, so she complains about the rain literally all the time, but honestly, I think I'd prefer constant rain to the humidity we get here in the summer. The humidity just ruins my hair the second I step outside, and then you're just sticky all day at the office. 

But um... what was I saying? Oh, right, enjoying things. Yeah, all those things I used to do, the hikes and the photos and the volunteering... now they just feel like items on a giant checklist. And I just... I don't care enough to even start them anymore.
Do you feel any pleasure when you do manage to complete a task or achieve something?

Pleasure? No, not at all. I mean, like I was just saying with the Sunday cooking and the photography and the hikes... it's all just a giant checklist that I don't even care enough to start. And on the rare occasion I actually force myself to finish something on it, there's no payoff. It's just a checked box. 

Which is really sad, actually, because I used to love it so much. I even have this beautiful Le Creuset Dutch oven for my Sunday meals. It's the cerise red one. I drove three hours to an outlet mall just to get it on sale a couple of years ago. The traffic was absolutely awful, and the parking lot was so packed I saw two grown adults literally screaming at each other over a space near the food court. I don't even know why everyone wants to park near the food court anyway, the only thing there is an Auntie Anne's pretzels. Have you ever tried to eat one of those in the car? They are so incredibly greasy, they completely ruin your steering wheel. My car has this nice leather wrap on the wheel that I really didn't want to ruin, so I had to use, like, five napkins... 

But um, sorry, what did you ask me? Right, feeling good when I finish a task. Yeah, no. Like I said, I don't even care enough to start most things anymore, let alone finish them.
Have you had any thoughts of not wanting to be alive or wishing you could just disappear?

Disappear? No... no, I haven't thought about, like, not being alive or anything. I mean, sometimes I wish I could just pause everything, or maybe go somewhere else for a while. Like, my uncle actually has this cabin up near Lake George. It's totally off the grid. He built the deck himself back in the 90s, which is pretty crazy because he's an orthodontist, not a carpenter. He used to make us go up there every summer when I was a kid, and the mosquitoes were literally the size of small birds. I swear, bug spray did absolutely nothing up there. We tried the citronella candles, DEET, even those weird little rubber bracelets they sell at the pharmacy... 

Which, by the way, the pharmacy near my apartment just completely changed their store layout and it makes absolutely no sense. They moved the toothpaste to the same aisle as the greeting cards. Who buys a birthday card and thinks, oh, I need Crest Whitestrips? It's completely illogical. I'm an auditor, so inefficient systems like that really bother me. I stood there for ten minutes the other day just looking for dental floss... 

But um, wait. Did you ask about the cabin? Oh, right, disappearing and not wanting to be alive. No, I don't want to die or anything like that. I just... I just don't have the energy for anything right now.
Do you feel anxious or worried about things more often than you used to?

Anxious? Um... no, not really. I mean, I'm not sitting around worrying about things. I just don't have the energy to care, honestly. It's funny you mention worrying, though, because my mom is the biggest worrier on the planet. I swear, she calls me every single time it rains because she thinks I'm going to hydroplane on my way to work. And my commute is literally ten minutes down a straight road. But she watches the Weather Channel like it's a soap opera. The other day she called me in a panic because there was a severe thunderstorm warning, and she started telling me about this special emergency radio she bought off QVC. She buys so much stuff from QVC. Last month it was this set of silicone baking mats that she swore were going to change my life, even though I just told you I don't even have the energy to cook anymore. 

Anyway, the delivery guy left the package out in the rain, and the cardboard got completely soggy. It was one of those boxes that just falls apart the second you try to pick it up, and little pieces of wet cardboard got all over my front steps. I had to sweep them up, which was so frustrating because the broom I have is one of those cheap plastic ones from the dollar store where the bristles just bend instead of actually sweeping anything...

Wait, sorry. What were we talking about? Worrying? Yeah, no. I'm not really anxious or worried about anything. Like I said, everything just feels completely flat. I don't care enough to be anxious.
Do you find yourself moving or speaking more slowly than you used to?

Slowly? Yeah, actually, that's kind of... that's a big part of what brings me in. I've gotten so slowed down lately. I'll just sit there staring at one single audit workpaper for like, twenty minutes before I even move my hand to type a single number. And people at work have definitely started noticing I'm not keeping up. My manager, Susan, actually pulled me aside the other day. She's usually really nice, she always brings in these amazing lemon bars on Fridays. She gets the recipe from her mother-in-law, who apparently lives in Savannah and has this huge Meyer lemon tree in her backyard. I tried growing a lemon tree once in my apartment, but it just completely died. I think it didn't get enough sunlight because my only good window faces an alleyway where they keep the dumpsters. 

The garbage trucks come at like 4 AM on Tuesdays and Thursdays, and they make this horrific crashing sound when they drop the metal bins back down. It wakes me up every single time, and then I just lie there listening to the street sweeper go by. The street sweeper has this really weird rhythmic hum to it, kind of like a washing machine that's off balance. My washing machine actually did that last week, it was shaking so hard I thought it was going to break right through the floorboards. I had to call maintenance, and the guy who showed up was wearing these bright orange Crocs, which I thought was a really bold choice for a maintenance worker...

But um, sorry. What was the question? Oh, moving slowly. Yeah, I'm just... I'm incredibly slow right now. Like I said, staring at the screen for twenty minutes before I can even type. It's really bad.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight recently?

Weight? Um... yeah, actually. My work skirts have gotten really loose lately, and I haven't been trying to lose weight at all. Food has mostly just become this thing I force down because I know I should. It's like chewing cardboard. Speaking of cardboard, remember I was telling you about that soggy box my mom's package came in? The delivery company they use is just terrible. The driver always parks right in front of the fire hydrant, which I'm pretty sure is highly illegal. I saw a guy get a ticket for doing that right outside my office building once. 

My office is downtown, right near this amazing little deli that used to make the best pastrami sandwiches. The owner was this guy named Sal, and he remembered everyone's order. He always knew I wanted extra pickles. But they closed down last year because the landlord jacked up the rent. It's happening to all the small businesses in that neighborhood. They replaced Sal's deli with one of those overpriced artisanal coffee shops where they charge you seven dollars for a latte and the baristas wear suspenders. I went in there once and asked for just a regular drip coffee, and the guy looked at me like I had insulted his ancestors. And they don't even have regular sugar packets, just this raw agave nectar stuff that comes in a tiny little glass bottle with a cork in it. I spilled it all over my hands and they were sticky for the rest of the day...

Wait, sorry. Did you ask about my weight? Yeah, my skirts are loose. I'm just not eating much, just forcing it down when I have to.
Do you feel worse in the morning?

Worse in the morning? Um... no, I don't think so. I mean, I feel pretty much the same awful way all day long. Getting out of bed is hard, but it's not like it gets any better by lunchtime. Speaking of lunchtime, they changed the cafeteria vendor at my building recently, and it's been a total disaster. They got rid of the salad bar and replaced it with this hot food station that always smells like old cooking oil. 

The woman who runs the register now is so incredibly slow, too. She has to look up the code for every single item. Last week, I was stuck behind this guy who was trying to pay for a banana with a hundred-dollar bill. Who carries a hundred-dollar bill for lunch? He had this really obnoxious leather wallet on a chain, which I haven't seen anyone wear since like, 1998. It reminded me of my cousin Joey, he used to wear those chain wallets when he was in his punk rock phase in high school. He actually dyed his hair bright green once using Kool-Aid, and it stained his pillowcases so badly my aunt made him sleep on towels for a month. Aunt Linda is super particular about her linens. She only buys Egyptian cotton, thread count of at least 800. She says anything less feels like sandpaper. I bought some cheap sheets from Target once when I first moved out, and honestly, they were fine, but they pilled up after like three washes...

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, mornings. Right. No, I don't really notice a difference. It's just all kind of a blur of feeling terrible, honestly.
Do you often feel guilty about things?

Guilty? Um... no, I don't think I feel guilty about anything in particular. I mean, I feel awful, but not really guilty. Well, maybe a little guilty about not calling my sister back on Sunday, but she always calls right when I'm trying to do my laundry. My apartment building has this shared laundry room in the basement, and it's a total nightmare. There are only four washers for the whole building, and one of them has been broken since November. It just has this piece of yellow caution tape slapped across it. 

The landlord, Mr. Henderson, is so cheap. He drives this immaculate vintage Mercedes, but he won't pay to fix a washing machine. I saw him polishing the hood of that car last weekend while I was carrying my laundry basket down the street to the laundromat. The laundromat is okay, I guess, but it always smells strongly of bleach and stale popcorn. They have this ancient popcorn machine in the corner that I don't think anyone has actually used in a decade. It's right next to this arcade cabinet of Pac-Man where the joystick is permanently stuck pointing left. I tried playing it once while waiting for my dryer to finish, and my little yellow guy just kept running into the wall over and over again until the ghosts got him. The ghosts have names, you know. Inky, Blinky, Pinky, and Clyde. Clyde always seemed like an odd name for a ghost. It sounds more like an accountant's name. Actually, there's a guy named Clyde in our tax department, and he wears these really aggressive plaid suits...

Wait, sorry. Did you ask if I felt guilty? Yeah, no, not really. Just the normal stuff, I guess. Nothing major.
Do you often feel like you're worthless or a burden to others?

Worthless? Um... no, I wouldn't say that. I don't really feel like a burden, either. I live alone, so there's not really anyone to be a burden to, you know? Just me and my plants. I have this one pothos plant that I've managed to keep alive for three years, which is a miracle because I usually have a black thumb. I bought it at this little farmer's market that sets up in the plaza near my office on Thursdays. 

They have this one stall that sells the most amazing local honey. The guy who runs it wears this big beekeeper hat, even though he's just selling jars of honey in the middle of the city. He told me once that the bees in urban areas actually produce better honey because they have a wider variety of flowers to pollinate from all the window boxes and parks. I tried to start a window box once, planted some basil and mint, but the pigeons absolutely destroyed it. Pigeons are so aggressive here. I saw one fighting a seagull over a french fry last week. The seagull was easily twice its size, but the pigeon was just relentless. It reminded me of this tiny little terrier mix my neighbor used to have. That dog would bark at anything that moved—cars, leaves, the mailman. The mailman actually started bringing dog treats just to bribe it so he could get to the mailboxes. He was a nice guy, the mailman. Always wore shorts, even in December. I don't understand how people can wear shorts in the winter. My legs get cold if it drops below sixty degrees...

Wait, sorry. Worthless? Burden? No, I don't feel like that. Just... empty, I guess. But not a burden.
Do you find yourself fidgeting or restless, having trouble sitting still?

Restless? Fidgeting? Um... no, not really. Actually, it's kind of the exact opposite. What brings me in is that I've gotten so slowed down lately. I can sit there staring at one single audit workpaper for like twenty minutes before I even move my hand to type. It's like I'm moving through molasses. And people at work have started noticing I'm not keeping up, which is stressful because it's almost tax season. 

Tax season is always a nightmare at our firm. We have this one client, a bakery downtown, and they bring in all their receipts in these giant, disorganized shoeboxes. Literally, Nike shoeboxes just stuffed with crumpled up pieces of paper. Some of them even have frosting stains on them. I don't know how they manage to run a business like that. The owner, this guy named Arthur, he always brings us a box of eclairs when he drops off the shoeboxes, I guess as an apology. The eclairs are amazing, though. They have this real vanilla bean custard inside, not that fake pudding stuff. I tried making custard from scratch once for Thanksgiving, and I completely scrambled the eggs. It was a disaster. My mom had to run to the grocery store at the last minute to buy a frozen pie. The grocery store on Thanksgiving morning is a wild place. People are practically fighting over the last can of cranberry sauce. I saw two women get into a shouting match over a bag of mini marshmallows...

Wait, sorry. What did you ask? Fidgeting? Yeah, no. I'm just... really, really slow. Not restless at all.
Do you feel significantly worse in the mornings, to the point where it's harder to get out of bed or start your day?

Mornings? Um... no, I wouldn't say the mornings are worse. It's pretty much the same all day. I mean, it is hard to get out of bed, but it's hard to do anything right now. My bed is actually pretty comfortable, though. I bought this memory foam mattress topper a few months ago, and it's supposed to have this cooling gel in it. I don't really know if the cooling part works, but it's definitely softer than my old mattress. I had my old mattress since college, which is probably gross to think about. 

I went to state for my undergrad, and the dorm beds were basically just plastic-covered bricks. We had to buy these egg-crate foam things just to sleep on them. My roommate freshman year, Sarah, she brought this huge, fluffy down comforter that took up half the room. She was from upstate, so she was always cold. She used to make hot chocolate in our tiny microwave every single night. The microwave always smelled faintly of burnt popcorn because some guy down the hall tried to pop a bag for like ten minutes on the first night of classes. The fire alarm went off at 2 AM, and we all had to stand out on the quad in our pajamas. It was September, so it wasn't freezing yet, but the grass was all wet with dew. I ruined my favorite pair of slippers that night. They were these fuzzy pink ones that looked like bunny rabbits. I tried putting them in the dryer to fix them, but the ears got all matted and weird...

Wait, sorry. Did you ask about mornings? Yeah, no, mornings aren't any worse than the rest of the day. It's just all kind of the same.
Have you ever felt like things would be better for the people around you if you weren't there?

Better if I wasn't here? Um... no, I don't think so. I mean, like I said earlier, I live alone, so it's not like I'm in anyone's way at home. And at work, even though I'm super slow right now, they'd probably just have to hire a temp if I left, and training temps is a huge hassle. We had this one temp last year during tax season, his name was Greg, and he kept putting the client files in alphabetical order by their first name instead of their last name. It took us like three weeks to find anything. 

He was a nice guy, though. He used to bring in these little bags of homemade trail mix for everyone. He said his wife made it. It had these little yogurt-covered raisins in it, which I usually hate, but hers were actually really good. I tried to buy some at the grocery store once, but they just tasted like chalk. The grocery store near my apartment is terrible anyway. They always run out of the weirdest things, like garlic powder or paper towels. Once, I went in there just to get some aluminum foil, and the entire aisle was empty. Just bare shelves. It looked like a hurricane was coming or something. The cashier told me there was a problem with the delivery truck, like it broke down on the highway and spilled a bunch of stuff. I hate driving on the highway. People go so fast, and no one uses their turn signals anymore. I got rear-ended once on my way to a client site because the guy behind me was texting. It completely crumpled my bumper, and the insurance company took forever to process the claim. I had to drive a rental car for a month, and it smelled like cheap vanilla air freshener...

Wait, sorry. What were we talking about? Oh, if things would be better if I wasn't around? No, I don't really think about that. I just... I don't really think I affect people that much either way.
Do you feel like you're unable to experience any positive emotions at all?

Positive emotions? Um... I don't know about not being able to experience them at all, but I definitely don't enjoy anything anymore. I used to do so much. I would plan these long hikes, take photos, cook big meals on Sundays, and volunteer at the local library. But now, those things just feel like items on a checklist I don’t care enough to start. 

The library was actually pretty interesting, though. I used to help reshelve the returns, which sounds boring, but there's something really satisfying about putting things in exact order. Well, mostly. Sometimes people would return books with the weirdest things used as bookmarks. Once I found a single slice of American cheese in a mystery novel. Like, still in the plastic wrapper, but totally squished and gross. Who uses cheese as a bookmark? It completely ruined the pages, obviously. The head librarian, Mrs. Gable, was so mad. She had this incredibly strict policy about food in the library because they had a terrible mouse problem a few years ago. She used to walk around with this little heavy-duty flashlight looking for cracker crumbs under the reading tables. She was terrifying, honestly. She wore these reading glasses attached to a pearl chain, and if you were talking too loud, she’d just drop the glasses onto her chest and glare at you until you stopped. I think she used to be a high school principal or something before she worked there. High school was so stressful. I was in the marching band, and we had to wear these heavy wool uniforms even during the summer band camp in August. One time, our tuba player passed out right in the middle of a Fourth of July parade. His tuba made this huge crashing sound on the asphalt...

Wait, sorry. What were you asking? Oh, positive emotions. Yeah, no. Like I said, the hikes and the cooking and volunteering... I just don't care about any of it anymore. It's just a checklist I can't bring myself to do.
Do you find it difficult to initiate or complete tasks due to feeling mentally or physically slowed down?

Slowed down? Yeah, actually, that's kind of what brings me in. I’ve gotten so slowed down lately. Like, I can sit staring at one audit workpaper for twenty minutes before I even move my hand to type. It's just... I just stare at the screen. We use this really outdated accounting software, and the background is this awful, dull gray color. It reminds me of the carpet in my first apartment. 

That place was so cheap, but the landlord refused to replace the carpets, so they had these weird, mysterious stains everywhere. I bought all these area rugs to cover them up. I got this one really pretty Persian-style rug at a flea market, but it turned out it was completely infested with carpet beetles. It was an absolute nightmare. I had to throw out half my clothes. The exterminator who came was this guy named Chuck, and he talked my ear off for two hours about his amateur bowling league. He was surprisingly passionate about bowling shoes. He said you should never rent them because of the bacteria, which, I mean, makes sense, but the way he described it was so graphic. I haven't been bowling since. I used to go for my birthday sometimes when I was a kid. We’d get those greasy arcade pizzas and play skee-ball until we had enough tickets for a plastic spider ring or a handful of Tootsie Rolls. I always choked on Tootsie Rolls...

Wait, sorry. Did you ask about being slowed down at work? Right. Yeah, um, people at the office have started noticing I’m not keeping up. It just takes me forever to even initiate a task or move my hands to type anything.
Do you feel like you're unable to concentrate or make decisions?

Concentrate? Um, I don't really think I have an issue with that. Or making decisions. I mean, I guess I haven't really had to make any big decisions lately. The biggest thing I had to decide recently was what kind of coffee to buy because my usual brand was sold out. They had this new hazelnut roast on sale, but I'm always so hesitant to try flavored coffees. Sometimes they just taste super artificial, you know? Like that fake cherry flavor they put in cough syrup. 

When I was little, I got sick all the time. I had strep throat like four times in one year, and my mom would always make me take that bright red liquid medicine. It was so thick and sticky. She used to promise me a popsicle afterward if I didn't spit it out. We always had those twin-pop ones, the ones that you can break in half. The grape ones were the best, but my brother always grabbed those first, so I usually ended up with orange. I don't really like orange-flavored things. Even orange juice... I can only drink it if it has zero pulp. Pulp just feels like you're drinking something that hasn't been finished yet. My ex-boyfriend used to buy the extra-pulp kind, and he'd just drink it straight out of the carton. It drove me absolutely crazy. He was so messy. He’d leave his socks everywhere, too. Just balled up under the coffee table or behind the couch...

Wait, what did you ask me? Oh, concentrating and making decisions. No, I don't think I have a problem with that. I just haven't had to make any big choices lately.
Have you experienced a loss of interest in activities you once enjoyed for more than two weeks?

Loss of interest for more than two weeks? Um, yeah, definitely. This has been going on for about seven months now. It started right around the time my husband stopped working after the downsizing at his company. 

The downsizing was so stressful. They just came in one Tuesday and handed out these generic manila folders to half the department. Manila folders always remind me of my high school guidance counselor. He had this massive filing cabinet that would always get stuck. He'd have to yank on the handle with both hands, and one time it tipped forward and spilled hundreds of those folders all over the linoleum floor. It took us like an hour to pick them all up, and all the papers got out of order. I hate when papers get out of order. I always keep my desk at home perfectly organized with these little acrylic trays. I found them at this container store that was going out of business. Going out of business sales are always so chaotic, though. People just tear through the aisles, leaving things wherever they want. I saw someone leave a half-eaten pretzel right on top of a stack of decorative storage boxes once. Who eats a pretzel while shopping for storage boxes? 

Wait, sorry. What were we talking about? Oh, right, how long it's been. Yeah, about seven months, since my husband got downsized.
Do you feel like your lack of interest in activities is worse in the morning?

Worse in the morning? Um, I don't know. I haven't really noticed if it's worse at any specific time of day. It just sort of feels the same all the time. But mornings are hard anyway, just getting out of bed. My alarm clock is so loud. It's one of those old digital ones with the bright red numbers that just blares at you. I bought it at a thrift store years ago because I liked the retro look, but the snooze button sticks. 

Thrift stores always smell so weird, don't they? Like mothballs and old dust. I used to go thrifting a lot with my college roommate, Sarah. She was obsessed with finding vintage denim jackets. She had this whole collection of them hanging in our tiny dorm closet. We lived in this older dorm building that didn't have air conditioning, so in September, it was just sweltering. We had these two little box fans that we kept running constantly, but all they did was blow hot air around. One time, someone burnt popcorn in the microwave down the hall, and the smell got sucked into our room and just lingered for days. Burnt popcorn is the absolute worst smell. It gets into everything. My dad used to make popcorn on the stove in this big metal pot, and he'd shake it back and forth over the burner. He always burned the bottom layer...

Wait, what was the question? Oh, if it's worse in the morning. No, I don't think so. I haven't really paid attention to the time of day, honestly.
Do you feel like your current state is severely impacting your daily life?

Impacting my daily life? Yeah, I guess it really is. Especially at work. I’m an auditor, and lately, I’ve just been missing review deadlines left and right. I’ve even had to hand off parts of audits that I usually manage all by myself. It’s embarrassing, honestly. And at home, it’s not much better. My husband has had to take over paying all the bills and dealing with the insurance forms because I just can’t reliably get through them anymore. 

Insurance forms are the absolute worst, aren't they? They use all this tiny print and confusing language. It reminds me of the terms and conditions you have to agree to when you download a new app on your phone. Who actually reads those? You just scroll to the bottom and click "agree." I did that once with this puzzle game app, and suddenly I was getting all these weird spam emails about discount vitamins. Vitamins are so expensive now. I used to buy those gummy ones because they taste like candy, but then I read an article saying they don't even have as many nutrients as the regular pills. The regular pills are so huge, though. They're like horse pills. My grandpa used to take these massive fish oil capsules, and he kept them in the refrigerator so they wouldn't taste fishy when they went down. Our refrigerator at home is making this weird humming noise lately. It sounds like a tiny airplane trying to take off. We probably need to call someone to fix it, but finding a good appliance repair person is so hard. You never know if they're going to overcharge you...

Wait, sorry. What did you ask me? Oh, right, impacting my daily life. Yeah, it definitely is. I'm just dropping the ball on my audits at work, and my husband is doing all the paperwork at home now.
Do you feel like you're unable to experience pleasure from activities you used to enjoy most of the day, nearly every day?

Most of the day, nearly every day? Yeah, that sounds about right. It's like... I used to do all these things, you know? I would plan these long weekend hikes, and I was always taking photos of everything, and I'd do this big Sunday meal prep, and I even volunteered at the local library sorting books. But now, it's all just... none of it matters. They just feel like items on a checklist that I don't even care enough to start. 

I used to love the library, though. The smell of old paper and the quiet. They had this one section in the back with all the local history archives, and the shelves were those metal ones that kind of squeaked when you rolled them on their tracks. Squeaky wheels drive me crazy. Like at the grocery store, when you get the one cart that has a wobbly wheel and it just clacks the whole time you're walking down the aisle. I always try to test them before I pull them out of the corral, but sometimes you get stuck with a bad one anyway. The grocery store near us just remodeled, and they moved everything around. They put the dairy where the bakery used to be, and it completely throws off my whole routine. I used to go in, grab bread, then produce, but now I have to zigzag across the entire store. Zigzagging is so inefficient. My husband says I'm too obsessed with efficiency, but as an auditor, it's literally my job to find inefficiencies. Like this one company we audited last year, they were still using paper ledgers for their petty cash. Paper ledgers in this day and age! It's just asking for someone to spill coffee on it and ruin a whole year's worth of records. Coffee stains are impossible to get out, especially on white fabric. I ruined my favorite silk blouse...

Wait, I lost my train of thought. What did you ask me? Oh, right, not enjoying things anymore. Yeah, I just don't have the energy or care to do any of the stuff I used to like. It's just a blank checklist now.

It took us like an hour to pick them all up, and all the papers got out of order. I hate when papers get out of order. I always keep my desk at home perfectly organized with these little acrylic trays. I found them at this container store that was going out of business. Going out of business sales are always so chaotic, though. People just tear through the aisles, leaving things wherever they want. I saw someone leave a half-eaten pretzel right on top of a stack of decorative storage boxes once. Who eats a pretzel while shopping for storage boxes? 

Wait, sorry. What were we talking about? Oh, right, how long it's been. Yeah, about seven months, since my husband got downsized.

doctor.intent: determine the presence of melancholic features
doctor.question: Do you feel like your lack of interest in activities is worse in the morning?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about diurnal variation (symptoms being worse in the morning), which is a specific melancholic feature not covered in my symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Worse in the morning? Um, I don't know. I haven't really noticed if it's worse at any specific time of day. It just sort of feels the same all the time. But mornings are hard anyway, just getting out of bed. My alarm clock is so loud. It's one of those old digital ones with the bright red numbers that just blares at you. I bought it at a thrift store years ago because I liked the retro look, but the snooze button sticks. 

Thrift stores always smell so weird, don't they? Like mothballs and old dust. I used to go thrifting a lot with my college roommate, Sarah. She was obsessed with finding vintage denim jackets. She had this whole collection of them hanging in our tiny dorm closet. We lived in this older dorm building that didn't have air conditioning, so in September, it was just sweltering. We had these two little box fans that we kept running constantly, but all they did was blow hot air around. One time, someone burnt popcorn in the microwave down the hall, and the smell got sucked into our room and just lingered for days. Burnt popcorn is the absolute worst smell. It gets into everything. My dad used to make popcorn on the stove in this big metal pot, and he'd shake it back and forth over the burner. He always burned the bottom layer...

Wait, what was the question? Oh, if it's worse in the morning. No, I don't think so. I haven't really paid attention to the time of day, honestly.

doctor.intent: Determine the severity of depressive episode
doctor.question: Do you feel like your current state is severely impacting your daily life?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: At work I’ve missed review deadlines and had to hand off parts of audits I normally manage myself, and at home my husband has taken over bills and insurance forms because I can’t reliably get through them.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about how my current state is severely impacting my daily life, which corresponds to functional impairment.

patient.answer:
Impacting my daily life? Yeah, I guess it really is. Especially at work. I’m an auditor, and lately, I’ve just been missing review deadlines left and right. I’ve even had to hand off parts of audits that I usually manage all by myself. It’s embarrassing, honestly. And at home, it’s not much better. My husband has had to take over paying all the bills and dealing with the insurance forms because I just can’t reliably get through them anymore. 

Insurance forms are the absolute worst, aren't they? They use all this tiny print and confusing language. It reminds me of the terms and conditions you have to agree to when you download a new app on your phone. Who actually reads those? You just scroll to the bottom and click "agree." I did that once with this puzzle game app, and suddenly I was getting all these weird spam emails about discount vitamins. Vitamins are so expensive now. I used to buy those gummy ones because they taste like candy, but then I read an article saying they don't even have as many nutrients as the regular pills. The regular pills are so huge, though. They're like horse pills. My grandpa used to take these massive fish oil capsules, and he kept them in the refrigerator so they wouldn't taste fishy when they went down. Our refrigerator at home is making this weird humming noise lately. It sounds like a tiny airplane trying to take off. We probably need to call someone to fix it, but finding a good appliance repair person is so hard. You never know if they're going to overcharge you...

Wait, sorry. What did you ask me? Oh, right, impacting my daily life. Yeah, it definitely is. I'm just dropping the ball on my audits at work, and my husband is doing all the paperwork at home now.

doctor.intent: Determine the severity of depressive symptoms
doctor.question: Do you feel like you're unable to experience pleasure from activities you used to enjoy most of the day, nearly every day?

target_item.name: Loss_of_Interest
target_item.manifestation: I used to plan hikes, take photos, cook on Sundays, and volunteer at the library, but now those things just feel like items on a checklist I don’t care enough to start.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the inability to experience pleasure from activities I used to enjoy, which matches the symptom of loss of interest.

patient.answer:
Most of the day, nearly every day? Yeah, that sounds about right. It's like... I used to do all these things, you know? I would plan these long weekend hikes, and I was always taking photos of everything, and I'd do this big Sunday meal prep, and I even volunteered at the local library sorting books. But now, it's all just... none of it matters. They just feel like items on a checklist that I don't even care enough to start. 

I used to love the library, though. The smell of old paper and the quiet. They had this one section in the back with all the local history archives, and the shelves were those metal ones that kind of squeaked when you rolled them on their tracks. Squeaky wheels drive me crazy. Like at the grocery store, when you get the one cart that has a wobbly wheel and it just clacks the whole time you're walking down the aisle. I always try to test them before I pull them out of the corral, but sometimes you get stuck with a bad one anyway. The grocery store near us just remodeled, and they moved everything around. They put the dairy where the bakery used to be, and it completely throws off my whole routine. I used to go in, grab bread, then produce, but now I have to zigzag across the entire store. Zigzagging is so inefficient. My husband says I'm too obsessed with efficiency, but as an auditor, it's literally my job to find inefficiencies. Like this one company we audited last year, they were still using paper ledgers for their petty cash. Paper ledgers in this day and age! It's just asking for someone to spill coffee on it and ruin a whole year's worth of records. Coffee stains are impossible to get out, especially on white fabric. I ruined my favorite silk blouse...

Wait, I lost my train of thought. What did you ask me? Oh, right, not enjoying things anymore. Yeah, I just don't have the energy or care to do any of the stuff I used to like. It's just a blank checklist now.

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits a persistent loss of interest in activities they once enjoyed, significantly impacting their daily life, and reports feeling slowed down, with no evidence of manic episodes or psychotic symptoms.
